lines.text: Chapter 1: The miles machine.
lines.say: Chapter one: the miles machine.

lines.text: Start with a mile. You think of it as a reward. To an airline, it's a product it sells.
lines.say: Start with a single mile. You think of it as a reward. To an airline, it's a product it sells.

lines.text: The biggest buyers are banks. They buy miles in bulk and hand them to cardholders as rewards.
lines.say: The biggest buyers are banks. They buy miles in bulk, then hand them out to cardholders as rewards.

lines.text: Now the accounting. When an airline sells a mile, it can't count all that cash as revenue right away.

lines.text: Chapter 2: Delta's $8 billion card.
lines.say: Chapter two: Delta's eight billion dollar card.

lines.text: Delta and American Express launched their card partnership back in 1996.
lines.say: Delta and American Express launched their card partnership back in nineteen ninety-six.

lines.text: In April 2019, they signed an 11-year renewal that runs through the end of 2029.
lines.say: In April twenty nineteen, they signed an eleven-year renewal that runs through the end of twenty twenty-nine.

lines.text: Here's what Amex paid Delta each year: $3.4 billion in 2018, climbing to $8.2 billion in 2025.
lines.say: Here's what Amex paid Delta each year: three point four billion dollars in twenty eighteen, climbing to eight point two billion in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: From 2019 to 2025, the payments doubled, from $4.1 billion to $8.2 billion.
lines.say: From twenty nineteen to twenty twenty-five, the payments doubled, from four point one billion dollars to eight point two billion.

lines.text: $8.2 billion divided by 365 days is about $22.5 million a day.
lines.say: Eight point two billion dollars divided by three hundred sixty-five days is about twenty-two and a half million dollars a day.

lines.text: That's about $936,000 an hour, every hour, all year long.

lines.text: Delta says it signed up more than 1 million new Amex cards in 2025, for the fourth year in a row.

lines.say: That's an estimated two hundred seventeen billion dollars of card spending. Eight point two billion divided by that is about three point eight cents per dollar.

post.title: In 2025, Delta's Amex deal beat its whole profit. How airlines make money from cards
post.ig: In 2025, Amex paid Delta $8.2B, more than Delta's $5.0B net income. Here's how airlines make money from credit cards.
post.tiktok: Amex paid Delta more than Delta's entire 2025 profit. Here's how airline cards work.
post.yt_desc:
How airlines make money from credit cards, not just flights. In 2025, American Express paid Delta $8.2 billion, more than Delta's $5.0 billion net income, and American Airlines received $6.2 billion from card and other partners while earning $111 million. This video covers how airlines sell miles to banks, how breakage and the accounting work, the math behind Delta's card deal (about $22.5 million a day), why United and American borrowed billions against their loyalty programs in 2020 and 2021, IATA's thin airline margins, and the risks: devaluation, the 2024 CFPB and DOT scrutiny of rewards, and the 2026 Credit Card Competition Act debate.
